vids.nm: Can a hero clean the air? 🌿
vids.desc: In this activity, students will create an animation where a “Clean Air Hero” takes action to reduce pollution in their surroundings. Using OctoStudio, they will design a scene where polluted air gets cleaned through actions like switching off smoke sources or activating clean elements like trees or wind. Students will understand the importance of clean air in fighting climate change while practising event-based coding, sequencing, and simple interactivity.

qs.q: Which block is used to change multiple scenes in one project in Octostudio?

opts.3: Switch Backdrop block

qs.q: What is the purpose of using the Send block in the animation creation process?

opts.1: To send a message allowing another sprite to take action
opts.3: To hide sprites from the screen

qs.q: If you want the girl's dialogue to appear on the screen for a specific time, which blocks would you use?

opts.3: Switch Backdrop and Hide blocks

qs.q: How can you creatively show the transition from a polluted to a clean environment using the tools mentioned in the script?

opts.1: Use a combination of Switch Backdrop, Say, and Send blocks to illustrate the change
opts.2: Use the Paint Editor to draw clouds
opts.3: Use only the Say block to describe the transition

qs.q: Imagine you want to add a new character that cleans the smoke faster. How would you creatively integrate this character using the existing blocks?

opts.1: Use the Send block to trigger the new character's action after smoke appears
opts.2: Use the Say block to introduce the character
opts.3: Use the Paint Editor to draw the character

vids.desc: Students will learn how to create an interactive game using OctoStudio to collect dripping water from taps, reinforcing the concept of water conservation. They will apply coding skills like using motion, broadcast, and sensing blocks while understanding the real-world relevance of SDG 6 – Clean Water and Sanitation. The activity promotes awareness that even small actions, like fixing leaks, can support a global cause. Through hands-on learning, students will combine creativity and problem-solving to build a meaningful digital solution.

vids.nm: Can Sunlight Make a Car Move? 🚗
vids.desc: Students will create a simple animation where a solar-powered car starts moving only when it receives energy from sunlight. Using OctoStudio, they will animate the sun, a solar panel attached to a car, and the car’s movement. This activity helps students understand how solar energy can be used in real-life applications like transport, while practising event-based coding and sequencing (SDG 7 & 13).
